problem: Stereo depth estimation fails in rapidly changing scenes with conventional frame-based cameras, and spike cameras lack specialized algorithms and benchmarks.
approach: SpikeStereoNet fuses raw spike streams from two viewpoints through a recurrent spiking neural network that iteratively refines depth estimation, trained on synthetic and real-world spike stream datasets.
contribution: Achieves superior depth estimation on both synthetic and real datasets while maintaining high accuracy with reduced training data.

problem: Current LLM benchmarks for competitive programming overstate model proficiency by using insufficiently difficult problems and low-quality test cases.
approach: AetherCode draws problems from premier competitions (IOI, ICPC) with expert-validated test suites created through hybrid automated generation and human curation.
contribution: Provides a more faithful measure of LLM reasoning capabilities than existing benchmarks with comprehensive, expert-validated evaluation.

problem: LLMs fail on tasks simple for humans due to biases from language structure; they miss implicit expressions that occur rarely during training.
approach: Constructs structural causal models of next-token predictors to show how language biases mislead LLMs, then proposes a prompt-level intervention instructing models to expand and focus on all available expressions.
contribution: Demonstrates that the prompt intervention improves performance across 11 tasks and 4 representative LLMs by helping models overcome language expression biases.

problem: Learning object-centric world models at scale from video data without supervision is challenging for decision-making applications.
approach: LPWM autonomously discovers keypoints, bounding boxes, and object masks from video, models stochastic particle dynamics via a latent action module, and supports flexible conditioning on actions, language, and image goals.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on diverse real-world and synthetic datasets while being applicable to goal-conditioned imitation learning.

problem: Large Reasoning Models produce overconfident incorrect answers instead of admitting ignorance, with pathological patterns like overthinking and second-thought spiraling.
approach: BARREL promotes concise and boundary-aware factual reasoning by training models to recognize reasoning boundaries and avoid overthinking patterns.
contribution: Increases reliability of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B from 39.33% to 61.48% while maintaining comparable accuracy to reasoning-data fine-tuned models.

problem: Role-playing agents fail to adapt personas to dynamic scenarios because persona influence on behavior varies contextually, unlike static prompt engineering or fine-tuning.
approach: PDD dynamically estimates context-dependent persona importance through a Persona Importance Estimation module and integrates it into weighted reward-guided decoding for inference-time adaptation.
contribution: Improves utterance consistency and behavioral fidelity by dynamically modulating persona influence based on scenario context.

problem: Verifying role-awareness in role-playing conversational agents is difficult because creative role-playing lacks clear, verifiable reward signals for reinforcement learning.
approach: VeriRole uses a 'hint' mechanism to extract deterministic contextual cues before response generation, then applies a Verifiable Role-Awareness Reward for RL training.
contribution: Achieves 18.9% improvement on RAIDEN and 4.55% on CharacterEval benchmarks for role-aware persona consistency.

problem: Neural VRP solvers assume symmetric Euclidean distances, restricting applicability to real-world asymmetric vehicle routing scenarios.
approach: RADAR augments neural VRP solvers using SVD on asymmetric distance matrices for compact initialization and Sinkhorn normalization for dynamic asymmetry modeling in attention.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, preserving model ranking at scale across various VRP types.

problem: Federated learning with Byzantine clients and heterogeneous data lacks robust defense mechanisms that jointly optimize aggregation weights and model parameters.
approach: Treats aggregation weights as learnable parameters jointly optimized with model parameters via alternating minimization, incorporating adaptive weighting into the FL objective.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing Byzantine-robust FL methods, particularly with highly heterogeneous data and large proportions of malicious clients.

problem: Existing adversarial scenario generators for autonomous driving use fixed trade-offs between adversariality and realism, lacking inference-time flexibility.
approach: SAGE reframes scenario generation as multi-objective preference alignment, training opposing expert policies and interpolating their weights at inference for continuous trade-off control.
contribution: Enables fine-grained test-time steering between adversariality and realism without retraining, improving closed-loop training effectiveness.

problem: SGD learning dynamics in sequential single-index model learning remain unexplored despite SGD's empirical success in feature learning.
approach: Analyzes SGD for single-index models under adaptive data, showing distinct burn-in and learning phases with appropriately chosen learning rate schedules.
contribution: Demonstrates that SGD simultaneously achieves near-optimal sample complexity and regret guarantees across both phases for a broad class of link functions.

problem: Adversarial prompt tuning for VLMs is limited by reliance on vulnerable continuous image features in the embedding space.
approach: DEFEAT reconstructs discrete latent features through a perturbation discrete shield module and designs a logits fusion strategy to reduce discrepancy between clean and adversarial representations.
contribution: Substantially improves adversarial robustness via discrete feature-based adversarial training across 15 datasets compared to existing prompt tuning methods.

problem: Growing benchmark suites make comprehensive LLM evaluation expensive; existing redundancy reduction methods lack systematic integration for both accuracy and ranking consistency.
approach: EssenceBench frames benchmark compression as an optimization problem using iterative Genetic Algorithm combining fitness-based subset search and attribution-based sample search.
contribution: Preserves model ranking with 25× fewer samples on HellaSwag and achieves 95% ranking preservation using 200× fewer samples.

problem: Decision making with structured observation has gaps between regret upper and lower bounds due to model estimation error scaling with model class size.
approach: Dig-DEC removes the optimism mechanism from prior work, aligning with model-based DEC while enabling seamless handling of adversarial environments.
contribution: Provides first model-free regret bounds in hybrid MDPs with bandit feedback for multiple settings including bilinear classes and Bellman-complete MDPs.

problem: Long-horizon stochastic optimal control scales linearly with horizon T and performance deteriorates exponentially for high-dimensional problems.
approach: For linearly-solvable SOC with gradient drift, reduces Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation to a linear PDE with discrete spectrum, enabling efficient long-horizon control via eigensystem learning.
contribution: Achieves order-of-magnitude improvement in control accuracy on long-horizon benchmarks while reducing memory usage and runtime from O(Td) to O(d).

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs suffers from high computational and memory costs due to verbose intermediate steps, while latent reasoning sacrifices clarity.
approach: HyRea enables dynamic switching between explicit token-based and latent embedding-based reasoning, trained via supervised cold-start and GRPO reinforcement learning.
contribution: Achieves significant reductions in token usage while maintaining or improving accuracy on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Existing causal discovery algorithms are slow or rely on continuous relaxations that fail to find optimal discrete graph structures.
approach: FLOP pairs fast parent selection with iterative Cholesky-based score updates and embraces discrete search via iterated local search with principled order initialization.
contribution: Achieves highly accurate structure recovery with near-perfect reconstruction in standard settings and substantially reduced runtime.

problem: Automated ethical benchmarking of autonomous systems is understudied due to lack of well-defined metrics and stakeholder-specific subjective value judgments.
approach: SEED-SET uses Bayesian experimental design to incorporate domain-specific objectives and subjective values via hierarchical Gaussian Processes with a novel acquisition strategy.
contribution: Generates up to 2× optimal test candidates with 1.25× improvement in high-dimensional search space coverage for ethical system evaluation.

problem: Online learning algorithms typically require numeric utility feedback, which is unavailable with human-in-the-loop systems or privacy concerns; ranking feedback is more practical.
approach: Studies online learning with ranking feedback models based on instantaneous or time-average utility, analyzing achievability of sublinear regret under various conditions.
contribution: Shows sublinear regret is impossible with instantaneous rankings; proposes algorithms for time-average rankings under additional assumptions on utility variation.

problem: Predictive models for invasive mechanical ventilation fail to generalize across multi-center ICU cohorts due to domain shifts from patient populations, practices, and EHR systems.
approach: AdaTTT enhances test-time training with self-supervised pretext tasks (reconstruction and masked feature modeling), prototype learning, and partial optimal transport for flexible feature alignment.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on multi-center adaptation benchmarks while maintaining clinically meaningful patient representations.

problem: Limited context windows of contemporary LLMs hinder broader application despite widespread need for longer context.
approach: SharedLLM uses two LLMs (compressor and decoder) with multi-grained context compression and query-aware retrieval via a tree-style data structure for efficient encoding and storage.
contribution: Achieves superior or comparable results to baselines on long-context tasks while reducing memory consumption and demonstrating substantial speed-ups.

problem: Video diffusion models struggle with multi-instance and subject-object interactions, lacking clear understanding of how they represent interactions.
approach: MATRIX analyzes interaction representation via semantic grounding and propagation in video DiTs, then applies regularization aligning specific layer attention with multi-instance mask tracks.
contribution: Improves interaction fidelity and semantic alignment while reducing drift and hallucination in interaction-aware video generation.

problem: Despite numerous hypergraph neural network proposals, absence of consistent experimental protocols and comprehensive benchmarks impedes understanding and development.
approach: DHG-Bench systematically evaluates 17 state-of-the-art HNN algorithms across 22 diverse datasets on node-, edge-, and graph-level tasks, analyzing effectiveness, efficiency, robustness, and fairness.
contribution: Provides comprehensive benchmark revealing strengths and limitations of existing algorithms and offers an easy-to-use library for reproducible HNN research.

problem: Understanding how hippocampal sequences arise in animal navigation remains elusive; current theories lack mechanistic explanation reconciling intrinsic dynamics with planning.
approach: Implements a minimal sequence generator inspired by neurobiology paired with an actor-critic learner for egocentric visual navigation, analyzing emergent place fields and spatial representations.
contribution: Shows that sparse input synergizes with sequence-generating dynamics to enable maze navigation, with emergent spatial phenomena aligning with neurobiological data.

problem: Offline RL methods require careful per-dataset hyperparameter tuning because policy constraint scales vary across datasets and qualities.
approach: ASPC provides a second-order differentiable framework that automatically adjusts policy constraint scales during training based on dataset characteristics.
contribution: Using a single hyperparameter configuration outperforms other adaptive methods and per-dataset-tuned algorithms, achieving 35% average improvement in normalized performance.

problem: Adversarial attacks on large VLMs often lack transferability to black-box models or produce easily detected artifacts.
approach: PSI uses diffusion-based progressive semantic infusion to align adversarial examples with natural image distribution and embed source-aware cues for stealthiness.
contribution: Effectively attacks open-source, adversarially trained, and commercial VLMs with superior transferability and stealthiness compared to existing methods.

problem: Multi-view clustering struggles to balance effectiveness, efficiency, completeness and consistency for nonlinearly separable data across multiple views.
approach: EKNN divides multi-view clustering into three sub-problems (linear, nonlinear, and integration) based on K-means and kernel K-means within a unified framework.
contribution: Balances all four criteria while achieving effectiveness and efficiency superior to other multi-view clustering methods.

problem: Prior work claims permutation search is necessary for linear mode connectivity; whether width alone suffices remains unclear.
approach: Demonstrates that widening models without permutations achieves LMC with softmax temperature calibration; explains via layerwise exponentially weighted connectivity (LEWC).
contribution: Shows that model width not only facilitates nonlinear mode connectivity but also significantly increases the possibility of achieving LMC.

problem: Speech tokenizers struggle to balance semantic understanding and acoustic reconstruction while achieving low bit rates and token rates.
approach: SiTok scales diffusion autoencoders to 1.6B parameters trained on 2 million hours of speech, jointly learning semantic representations and enabling high-fidelity reconstruction.
contribution: Outperforms baselines on reconstruction and understanding tasks at an extremely low token rate of 12.5 Hz and 200 bits-per-second.

problem: Current personalized long-form generation methods use static one-shot reasoning, limiting adaptability to evolving content and contextual changes.
approach: FlyThinker employs concurrent token-level reasoning generation and fusion, where reasoning depends on previous responses to enable dynamic guidance during generation.
contribution: Achieves better personalized generation while maintaining training and inference efficiency through parallel reasoning and generation.

problem: Dataset distillation may transfer memorized information from teachers to students through soft labels, raising privacy concerns about held-out data leakage.
approach: Studies whether students trained on soft labels from teachers can learn held-out memorized data they never observed, analyzing this on random i.i.d. datasets.
contribution: Shows that students can achieve non-trivial accuracy on held-out memorized data, demonstrating a privacy vulnerability in knowledge distillation.

problem: The representational role of signed weights in artificial and biological intelligence remains unclear despite their centrality to both systems.
approach: Uses sign consistency as proxy for biological Dale's law to investigate how signed weights shape visual representations, analyzing positive and negative weight contributions separately.
contribution: Reveals functional segregation where positive weights encode object features while negative weights capture background textures, with stronger effects in robust models.

problem: Optimizing discrete-valued scientific designs is combinatorially challenging; existing methods fail to leverage decomposability structure in property predictors.
approach: DADO proposes a distributional optimization algorithm that leverages decomposability defined by junction trees on design variables using a factorized search distribution.
contribution: Enables efficient navigation of design spaces by exploiting decomposable structure in property predictors.

problem: Continual RL requires knowledge transfer and integration while minimizing catastrophic forgetting; standard multi-task approaches fail to do both effectively.
approach: Proposes a dual-learner framework with a fast learner for transfer and meta learner for integration, inspired by hippocampus-cortex interplay, with adaptive meta warm-up.
contribution: Demonstrates superior performance on pixel-based and continuous control benchmarks for efficient cumulative knowledge transfer.

problem: Speculative sampling strictly enforces verifier distribution match, unnecessarily restricting acceptable sampling variations and acceptance rates.
approach: Cactus formalizes speculative sampling as constrained optimization, enabling controlled divergence from verifier distribution with entropy-based guarantees.
contribution: Increases acceptance rates while guaranteeing controlled distribution divergence, improving decoding throughput across diverse benchmarks.

problem: Axis-aligned decision trees are fast but struggle on datasets with rotated boundaries requiring feature interactions; oblique forests are computationally expensive.
approach: JARF applies a single global rotation via Jacobian-based preconditioning to axis-aligned random forests, capturing oblique boundaries without per-node hyperplane splits.
contribution: Matches or surpasses oblique baselines while training faster on tabular benchmarks.

problem: High-performance visual trackers are slow, limiting practical deployment on resource-constrained devices despite need for real-time tracking.
approach: FARTrack uses task-specific self-distillation and inter-frame autoregressive sparsification for model compression and efficient temporal token optimization.
contribution: Achieves 70.6% AO on GOT-10k in real-time with speeds of 343 FPS on GPU and 121 FPS on CPU.

problem: LLMs are impractical for edge deployment due to severe memory bottlenecks from large model sizes and KV-cache storage.
approach: ELMs replace groups of Transformer layers with lightweight fixed-point networks via Group Pruning Policy Optimization and One-Step KV-Cache for memory-efficient deployment.
contribution: Prunes 28% of parameters while retaining 99% accuracy, establishing a new direction for edge-deployable large models.

problem: LLM pruning with n:m semi-structured sparsity faces a trade-off between efficient one-shot approaches and accurate but expensive optimization methods.
approach: HyperPrune uses a lightweight shared hypernetwork conditioned on learnable embeddings to generate structured masks with continual pruning and feature outlier regularization.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy-sparsity trade-offs on LLaMA 7B-70B with higher efficiency, accuracy, and scalability than prior approaches.

problem: Understanding how Transformers leverage unlabeled context for representation learning in in-context learning settings with sparse labels is unexplored.
approach: Introduces in-context semi-supervised learning (IC-SSL) studying how Transformers exploit unlabeled demonstrations to learn robust context-dependent representations.
contribution: Shows Transformers can leverage unlabeled context to improve performance in low-label regimes, providing foundational insights into ICL representation learning.
